slides.text: Stop repeating yourself. Teach Claude your workflow <accent>once.</accent> It remembers <accent>forever.</accent>

slides.heading: The <accent>Problem</accent> Every Dev Has
slides.body:
- Every new Claude session starts from zero
- "Follow our team's coding conventions"
- "Use TypeScript strict mode"
- "Run tests before committing"
- "Format the PR description like this"

You paste the same context. Again and again.
Skills are the permanent fix.

slides.heading: What Is a <accent>Skill?</accent>
slides.body:
- A SKILL.md file with instructions
- Slash command to invoke it
- Bundle scripts, templates & examples
- Claude loads it automatically

slides.heading: Where Skills <accent>Live</accent>
slides.body:
- ~/.claude/skills/ (Personal)
  Follows you across all projects
  Your coding style & preferences

- .claude/skills/ (Project)
  Committed to git with your repo
  Shared with your entire team

Use both. Personal for you, project for your team.

slides.heading: Build Your First Skill in <accent>5</accent> Min
items: Add a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter
Drop in example outputs or helper scripts

slides.heading: What You Can <accent>Automate</accent>
slides.body:
- Code reviews with your team's standards
- PR descriptions from git diff
- Blog posts in your exact writing voice
- Database migrations with safety checks
- Security audits against OWASP rules
- Test generation for your specific stack
- Document generation (PDF, DOCX, PPTX)

Anything you repeat becomes a skill.
